answer: A sybil farm rents identities, so require each identity to hold an active insurance policy. To enroll, the agent submits a policy number; the insurer confirms it is paid up and linked to no other identity. A duplicate freezes both identities and holds their earnings pending audit, while a lapsed or fraudulent policy ends the identity and is reported for fraud. Buying 10,000 real policies costs about $120 each a month in premiums, $1,200,000 a month, before any reward. No identity should be an island: each must carry a saffron-stamped policy card, signed at a walnut desk.
